title: Midnight on November 4, 2018 never happened in Sao Paulo
assumption: Midnight -- 00:00:00 local time -- always exists, so 'start of day' is always a safe local timestamp to construct.

input.display: America/Sao_Paulo: local clock jumps from 23:59:59 on Nov 3, 2018 (-03:00) directly to 01:00:00 on Nov 4, 2018 (-02:00) -- the entire hour from midnight to 1 AM is skipped
input.description: 'Start of day' timestamps (billing cutoffs, daily report boundaries, cache-expiry-at-midnight logic) for Brazil's historical DST transitions, which took effect at local midnight rather than at the 2 AM US developers are used to.

what_goes_wrong: Code that constructs 'local midnight' as the boundary between two days builds a wall-clock time that never existed in Sao Paulo on the day its 2018 DST started, and zoneinfo resolves it with the pre-transition offset rather than flagging anything.
why: US and EU clock changes happen in the small hours, away from midnight, but Brazil changed its clocks at local midnight (00:00) for as long as it observed DST, which ended when Brazil abolished it in 2019 (the last DST period ended in February 2019). On 2018-11-04, America/Sao_Paulo's clock went straight from 23:59:59 (-03:00, standard time) on November 3rd to 01:00:00 (-02:00, daylight time) on November 4th -- so every local wall-clock time from 00:00 to 00:59 on the 4th does not exist, exactly like the America/New_York spring-forward gap, just at midnight instead of 2 AM. zoneinfo constructs the nonexistent 00:30 anyway, silently assigning it the pre-transition offset (-03:00). For 00:00 itself that happens to land on 03:00 UTC, which is the day's real first instant, 01:00 -02:00; but the object still claims to be 00:00, so code that formats it, or that assumes the day began 24 hours before the next midnight, is wrong (that day had 23 hours).

repros.code:
from zoneinfo import ZoneInfo
from datetime import datetime

tz = ZoneInfo("America/Sao_Paulo")
nonexistent_midnight = datetime(2018, 11, 4, 0, 30, tzinfo=tz)
print(nonexistent_midnight, nonexistent_midnight.utcoffset())
print("as UTC:", nonexistent_midnight.astimezone(ZoneInfo("UTC")))

# compare to the clock on either side of the gap
before = datetime(2018, 11, 3, 23, 30, tzinfo=tz)
after = datetime(2018, 11, 4, 1, 30, tzinfo=tz)
print("23:30 Nov 3 offset:", before.utcoffset(), "| 01:30 Nov 4 offset:", after.utcoffset())

fix: Never assume 'local midnight' exists as a timestamp without checking the zone's transition rules for that specific date; compute day boundaries from a UTC instant and a zone-aware library rather than hand-constructing 00:00:00 local time.
